title: connection quiesce window and soft-shed overprovision repair
author: Anika Patel
description: Motivation: During a recent multi-region traffic surge we observed a class of incidents where 'soft-shed' heuristics overestimated available overprovision when many connections entered short-lived transient states. The result was repeated premature shedding followed by rapid reopen cycles and elevated tail-latency for a subset of tenants. This PR introduces a connection quiesce window state and tightens the soft-shed overprovision accounting to avoid double-counting transient slots. The change is intentionally conservative: it aims to reduce oscillation while preserving overall throughput. Summary of changes: - Introduce a QuiesceWindow state machine in runtime/eviction to mark recently-closed connections as quiescent for a short configurable window (default 5s). - Adjust soft-shed overprovision estimator to exclude quiescent slots from being considered immediately available. - Add telemetry hooks and a new metric quiesce_window_active_count and shed_estimator_overprovision_delta for post-deploy validation. - Integration test that simulates bursty connection churn and validates stable shed decisions. - Operational playbook and runbook notes describing mitigation knobs and recommended rollout steps. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for state transitions - [x] Integration test for end-to-end behavior under bursty load - [x] Telemetry added and wired to Console dashboards - [x] Docs/runbook added - [x] Load test sanity on perf lab (local) Rollout plan: Stage rollout to 10% of instances in us-west-2 for 2 hours, monitor quiesce_window_active_count and shed_estimator_overprovision_delta; then ramp if no regressions. Related: ENG-2145 for a follow-up to add per-tenant quiesce tuning. Backport: hotfix branch applied to release/2026-02 for immediate mitigation.
